title: Light and electron microscopic imaging of synaptic vesicle endocytosis at mouse hippocampal cultures
protocol: Sterilize tools with 70% ethanol 30 min before dissection.
Transfer 10–15 mL of ice-cold Dissection Solution to each of four 60-mm Petri dishes.
Decapitate a P0‒P1 pup with angled scissors.
Keep the head in the first dish on a frozen-cold metal plate to maintain the Dissection Solution cool.
Precool 3–4 metal plates in a −20°C freezer for 2–3 hours before dissection.
Replace the plate under the dish with one precooled from the freezer every 10–15 minutes.
Remove the scalp using two tweezers.
Pin down the head by impaling the eyes with blunt tweezers.
Make a small incision at the midline between the eyes with the tip of another curved tweezers.
Open the skull along the midline between the incision and the foramen magnum, keeping cuts shallow to avoid damaging the brain.
Remove the two halves of the skull using tweezers.
Separate the brain from the skull base.
Transfer the isolated brain to the second dish.
Hold the brainstem with blunt tweezers under the dissection microscope (1×).
Remove cerebral hemisphere with fine tweezers.
Gently peel off meninges surrounding the hippocampus with fine tweezers.
The hippocampus, a C-shaped structure, should be clearly visible.
Pin down the cerebral cortex using blunt tweezers.
Isolate the hippocampus along its convex side with fine tweezers.
Transfer the hippocampal tissue to the third dish using a cut 1-mL pipette tip.
Cut off the remaining dentate gyrus and subiculum around the hippocampus with fine scissors.
Transfer the cleaned hippocampal tissue to the fourth dish.
Chop each hippocampus into 5–10 pieces with fine scissors.
Transfer all chopped tissues into a 15-mL tube using a 1-mL tip.
Wash the tissues twice with 10 mL of ice-cold HBSS (with Ca2+ and Mg2+).
Remove 90% of the ice-cold HBSS from the tissue.
Transfer the hippocampal tissue to a 15-mL tube containing 5 mL of 37°C Papain Solution using a 1-mL tip.
Incubate the tissue in a 37°C incubator for 45 min, shaking gently occasionally.
Prepare the 1/1 Solution and 10/10 Solution during the digestion period.
Sterilize tweezers by passing them through a flame.
Place a 25-mm coverslip coated with mouse laminin and poly-D-lysine in each well of a 6-well plate using sterilized tweezers.
Keep the plate in the 37°C incubator until cell plating.
Transfer the hippocampal tissue to a 15-mL tube containing 2 mL of 1/1 Solution to stop digestion.
Use a 1-mL tip to triturate the digested tissue 2–3 times.
Allow the tissue to settle to the bottom of the tube before each trituration.
Gently pipette the suspension up and down 5 times until all pieces are broken up uniformly.
Triturate the tissue until the suspension appears cloudy without any large pieces.
Triturate the suspension two more times until it appears cloudy without any large pieces left.
Set the desired volume of a 1-mL pipette gun to 750 μL.
Depress the plunger to the first stop and immerse the tip in the solution.
Firmly push the tip against the bottom of the tube, then tilt the tip at a small angle to form a narrow gap between the bottom of the tube and the tip edge.
Release the depressed plunger slowly to aspirate tissues into the tip through the tight gap.
Gently depress the plunger to push the suspension out of the tip.
Repeat trituration 2–3 times until large pieces of tissue disappear.
Spin down the suspension at 100 × g for 5 min at RT (22°C–24°C).
Carefully aspirate off 95% of the supernatant.
Resuspend the pellet with 2 mL of 1/1 Solution using a 1-mL tip, pipetting up and down 5 times until the pellet is completely dissociated.
Allow the suspension to settle for 10 min at RT in the tissue culture hood.
Gently remove 95% of the supernatant.
Layer the remaining suspension on the surface of 10 mL of 10/10 Solution in a 15-mL tube while rotating the tube to achieve an even distribution.
Spin down the sample at 100 × g for 10 minutes at room temperature.
Remove 98% of the supernatant.
Resuspend the pellet with 3 mL of Plating Medium.
Pipette up and down 5 times to mix thoroughly.
Add 10 μL of the cell suspension to the hemocytometer.
Count cells in each of four square chambers under a light microscope (10×).
Estimate the total yield using the mean value from the counted cells.
Use Plating Medium to make up a suspension of 3.0 × 10^5 cells/mL or 4.0 × 10^5 cells/mL for EM.
Add 2 mL of cell suspension to each well of a 6-well plate (1 mL/well for a 12-well plate, 0.5 mL/well for a 24-well plate).
Ensure the entire coverslip is covered by the suspension in each well.
Maintain cells in a 5% CO2, 37°C incubator from day of plating to DIV21.
Check cells under light microscope (10×) every 2-3 days.
Feed cells every 3-4 days by replacing 50% of the medium with pre-warmed Feeding Medium.
At DIV0, plate the cells.
Add Cytosine β-D-arabinofuranoside (Ara-C) to the medium at a final concentration of 2–3 μM to limit proliferation of glial cells between DIV2‒DIV3.
Transfect the cells with synaptophysin-pHluorin (SypH) using Lipofectamine as a carrier at DIV7.
Discard remaining coverslips after DIV21 due to decline in neuron health and SypH expression.
Make Medium A by mixing 150 μL of Opti-MEM medium, 4 μL of Lipofectamine PLUS reagent, and 2 μg of SypH plasmid DNA in a 15-mL tube (for double transfection, add 1.5 μg for each plasmid).
Make Medium B by mixing 150 μL of Opti-MEM medium with 4 μL of Lipofectamine LTX reagent in a 15-mL tube.
Incubate Medium A and B at room temperature (RT) for 5 min; then mix them to make plasmid medium.
Incubate the plasmid medium at RT for 15–20 min in the tissue culture hood.
Transfer 1 mL/well of medium from the plate containing coverslip-plated neurons to corresponding wells of a new plate.
Add 1 mL/well of fresh Feeding Medium to Plate #1 and Plate #2.
Incubate each well in Plate #1 and Plate #2 with 2 mL medium (1 mL old medium and 1 mL fresh medium).
Add 300 μL/well of plasmid medium to Plate #1.
Incubate the plate for 40 minutes at 37°C.
Transfer coverslips from Plate #1 to corresponding wells in Plate #2 using flame-sterilized forceps.
Incubate Plate #2 in a 37°C, 5% CO2 incubator.
Monitor the expression level of SypH in neurons under a fluorescent microscope.
Prepare for imaging experiments at DIV13-15 when neurons are mature.
Use Nikon Eclipse Ti-E microscope and Andor camera (iXon X3 897 EMCCD) to study endocytosis at live individual boutons by monitoring changes in fluorescent signal.
Setup microscope settings for detecting the SypH signal.
Select an oil objective (60 ×, 1.4 NA).
Add a drop of immersion oil (Nikon, Type F).
Configure the software (NIS-Elements AR 5.20.02).
Set the exposure time as 100 ms and exposure frequency as 10 Hz.
Set the gain of A/D converter as 1, pixel readout rate as 10 MHz, pixel depth as 14-bit.
Set pixels binning for capture at no binning and “Live” window at 2 × 2.
Configure time-lapse imaging to cover fluorescence activities in resting condition (0-30 s), during stimulation (30-40 s), and recovery after stimulation (40-180 s).
Simultaneously export a trigger signal to the stimulator when acquisition starts.
Generate a train stimulation of 20 mA with 200 pulses at 1 ms each, delivered at 20 Hz.
Smear high-vacuum silicone grease on the bottom of the chamber.
Smear high-vacuum silicone grease on the top of the platform.
Mount a coverslip with plated neurons on the top of the platform.
Cover the coverslip with the chamber.
Gently press on the chamber to ensure a tight seal.
Add 250 μL of Saline Solution to bath.
Keep 100–200 μL of Feeding Medium on the coverslip.
Place a clamp on the top of the chamber and tighten the screws to fix the chamber.
Add 250 μL of saline solution to the chamber.
Dry the bottom side of coverslip with kimwipes.
Position and fix the coverslip-chamber unit on the stage of the microscope.
Connect the chamber to the output wires from the stimulus isolation unit for field stimulation.
Switch off epifluorescence light temporarily during neuron examination.
Identify neurons with round or oval fluorescent signals in boutons and dim, blurry, continuous signals in branches as good candidates for the experiment.
Discard neurons if they show bright, sharp, discontinuous signals indicating unhealthy cells or death.
Mark 20–50 expected boutons with 2 μm × 2 μm square markers on inactive “Live” window for later identification through fluorescence intensity changes upon stimulation.
Observe dimming of fluorescent signals as a potential indicator of bleaching due to intensive stimulation or unhealthy cell status from knock-out mice.
Discard coverslip after the first round of stimulation if issues arise with signal dimming.
Double-check focus by observing active “Live” window before starting data acquisition.
Start an acquisition based on changes in fluorescence intensity within marked squares indicating bouton activity and observe effects on endocytosis rate.
Collect fluorescence intensity traces from 5 corresponding ROIs.
Measure baselines from 0 to 30 seconds.
Increase stimulation with 200 1-ms pulses at 20 Hz from 30 to 40 seconds.
Monitor signal decay after 40 seconds, reflecting endocytosis.
Check system for proper delivery of stimulation if boutons do not respond.
Try another coverslip if stimulation is not delivered properly.
Identify and mark boutons with square markers (2 μm × 2 μm ROI).
Ensure each ROI is large enough to cover the largest changes in fluorescence.
Randomly select more than 20 boutons in one field of view for data analysis per experiment.
Exclude recordings if fewer than 20 boutons are visible in one field of view.
Increase cell density during plating or use additional cultures if necessary.
Do not collect data generated by multiple rounds of stimulation in different fields of view.
Use the same stimulation, exposure time, and intensity of epifluorescent light as previous studies.
Exclude affected boutons from analysis if bleaching occurs during stimulation.
Improve SypH expression in cultured neurons by increasing plasmid amount or using different carriers.
Select an area around a marked bouton for background fluorescence estimation.
Mark the selected area with a square marker (2 μm × 2 μm).
Choose about 20 background areas per experiment, each corresponding to a different marked bouton.
Export averaged data of bouton and background signals to Excel.
Calculate normalized ΔF (%) using the formula: Normalized ΔF (%) = ((Fmax - Fbaseline) / (Fbaseline - Fbackground)) × 100.
Conduct about 10 independent experiments from 3 cultures per experimental condition.
Measure endocytosis initial rate (Ratedecay).
Quantify fluorescence decay during the first 4-10 seconds after stimulation to measure endocytosis rate.
In Igor software, calculate the initial rate of endocytosis using a sampled trace.
Induce exocytosis and endocytosis with a train stimulation consisting of 200 1-ms pulses at 20 Hz.
Measure fluorescence response in WT boutons (n=17) and Kv3.3 KO boutons (n=15) at 34-37°C.
Summarize the Rate Decay values for WT and Kv3.3 KO conditions.
Calculate Rate Decay using the change in fluorescence density within 4-10 seconds after stimulation.
Determine that a smaller Rate Decay value indicates slower endocytosis.
Determine if mutation affects endocytosis by comparing the value of Ratedecay of the control group with that of the mutation group.
Observe the formation of individual vesicles and endosomes from the plasma membrane under an electron microscope for studying endocytosis.
Apply horseradish peroxidase (HRP) for 1.5 minutes during the application of a 90 mM K+ solution to label endocytosed vesicles.
In resting condition, add HRP for 1.5 minutes before fixation.

Include four preconditions before adding a fixative: resting condition without 90 mM K+ stimulation; no recovery condition with 90 mM K+ stimulation for 1.5 min only; short recovery condition with 90 mM K+ stimulation for 1.5 min and 3 min recovery after KCl washout; long recovery condition with 90 mM K+ stimulation for 1.5 min and 10 min recovery after KCl washout.
Add 300 μL of filtered poly-L-lysine solution to each well of the 24-well plate.
Incubate the plate at 37°C for 2 h.
Aspirate the poly-L-lysine solution.
Wash the plate 3 times with sterilized water for 10 min each.
Air dry for 30 min in the tissue culture hood, store in the 37°C incubator, and start the dissection.
Add 0.5 mL of the cell suspension (4.0 × 10^5 cells/mL) to each well of a 24-well plate.
Store the plate in the 5% CO2, 37°C incubator.
Transfect the Cre gene into hippocampal neurons using adeno-associated virus (AAV) carrier at DIV7 in conditional knockout mice.
Dilute glutaraldehyde from 70% to 4% by adding 0.1 M sodium cacodylate buffer (pH 7.4).
Dilute glutaraldehyde from 70% to 2% by adding 0.1 M sodium cacodylate buffer (pH 7.4).
Transfer all culture medium in the 24-well plate containing plated neurons (Plate #1) to corresponding wells of a new 24-well plate (Plate #2).
Add 300 μL of HRP Saline Solution to each well of Plate #1 for 1.5 min at room temperature.
Aspirate the HRP Saline Solution and wash cells with 500 μL of PBS.
Aspirate the PBS and add 500 μL of 4% glutaraldehyde to fix the cells.
Add 300 μL of HRP 90 mM KCl Solution to each well of Plate #1 for 1.5 min at room temperature.
Aspirate the HRP 90 mM KCl Solution and wash cells with 500 μL of PBS once to stop depolarization completely.
After aspirating the PBS, add 500 μL of 4% glutaraldehyde to fix the cells immediately.
Transfer the culture medium back from the wells of Plate #2 to the corresponding wells of Plate #1 for a 3 min recovery (condition 3) or 10 min recovery (condition 4).
Replace the culture medium in the wells of Plate #1 with 500 μL of 4% glutaraldehyde to fix the cells.
Incubate the plates with 4% glutaraldehyde for 2 hours at room temperature in a fume hood.
Wash the fixed cells with 500 μL of 0.1 M sodium cacodylate buffer three times.
Store the plate at 4°C overnight (12 h).
Allow the plate to equilibrate to room temperature.
Stain the fixed cells with 500 μL of DAB Solution at 37°C for 30 minutes.
Wash the fixed cells three times with 500 μL of 0.1 M sodium cacodylate buffer for 7 minutes each.
Aspirate the sodium cacodylate buffer and add 500 μL of 2% glutaraldehyde.
Temporarily store the plate at 4°C before post-fixation.
Remove 2% glutaraldehyde.
Wash fixed cells three times with 500 μL of 0.1 M sodium cacodylate buffer for 7 min each.
Incubate the fixed cells in 1% OsO4 (in 0.1 M sodium cacodylate buffer) on ice for 1 h, covered with foil.
Wash the samples three times with 500 μL of 0.1 M sodium cacodylate buffer on ice for 7 min each.
Incubate the samples with 500 μL of 0.25% uranyl acetate (UA, in 0.1 N sodium acetate buffer) for 1 h at 4°C, covered with foil.
Wash the samples three times with 500 μL of 0.1 N sodium acetate buffer for 7 min each.
Dehydrate the samples with 500 μL of 50%, 70%, and 90% ethanol in a fume hood for 7 min each.
Wash the samples three times with 500 μL of 100% ethanol for 7 min each.
Replace the water content in the samples with ethanol to allow resin infiltration.
Incubate the samples with 500 μL of 1:1 epoxy resin/ethanol on a rocker plate for 30 min at room temperature.
Incubate the samples with 500 μL of 2:1 epoxy resin/ethanol on a rocker plate for 30 min at room temperature.
Incubate the samples with 500 μL epoxy resin in a 50°C oven for 10 min.
Exchange epoxy mixture with fresh 100% epoxy resin and incubate at 50°C for 1 hour.
Repeat exchanging epoxy mixture with fresh 100% epoxy resin and incubating at 50°C for another 1 hour.
Add 500 μL of fresh epoxy resin and allow to harden in a 50°C oven overnight (12 hours).
Incubate the hardened sample in a 60°C oven for 48 hours.
Carefully select a region of interest (ROI) with plenty of neurites under an inverted light microscope.
Saw out the selected ROI and surrounding area from the plastic bottom of the plate using a jeweler’s saw.
Remove the sawed-out sample from the plastic bottom using a pair of pliers.
Place the sample on a chuck holder in an ultramicrotome (Leica Ultracut S).
Manually trim the sample to a trapezoid shape, with less than ∼0.5 mm wide and ∼1 mm long on the face side.
Section the sample extremely thinly (∼70 nm thick) using a diamond knife.
Collect sections on individual grids (400 mesh copper grid).
Air dry the collected grids overnight (12 h).
Stain the grids with 3% lead citrate for 5 min to enhance contrast.
Wash the grids with ddH2O for 10–12 s.
Wick dry them with filter paper.
Air dry the grids.
Examine the images with a transmission electron microscope (JEOL JEM-200CX, 120 kV).
Record the images with a CCD digital camera (AMT XR-100) at a magnification of 10,000–38,000×.
Set the EM magnification at: 100–1000× to find the sections on the grid.
Set the EM magnification at: 1000–5000× to choose the cells.
Set the EM magnification at: 10000–38,000× to image the boutons.
Set exposure time as 60 ms.
Set pixel binning as 4 × 4.
Set gain of the A/D converter as 2.
Set image average value as 2.
Collect digital images of synaptic boutons from different sections.
Ensure a clear presynaptic and postsynaptic structure is visible in the photo.
Zoom in on vesicles in the presynaptic part to confirm they have a round shape and clear membrane structure.
Measure the area of boutons and HRP (+) bulk endosomes.
Count the number of HRP (+) vesicles.
Calculate the number of HRP (+) vesicles per bouton (μm²).
Calculate the HRP (+) bulk endosome area per bouton (μm²).
Through analysis of the data, estimate the speed of vesicle endocytosis and bulk endocytosis.
If the number of HRP (+) vesicles per bouton (μm2) obtained from mutated cells after application of high K+ is less than that from wild-type cells, vesicle endocytosis may be inhibited by mutants.
To confirm changes in endocytosis induced by mutants, conduct additional experiments such as rescue experiments.
